date_note: The day ANSPDCP published its press release; the page gives no earlier day for the fine, says the investigation was completed in October 2026 and gives no date for the ransomware attack.
exec: Romania's regulator fined a spa hotel operator after a ransomware attack it says came through a remote connection without multi-factor authentication.
plain: Romania's data protection authority fined a hotel company in Băile Felix 26.649 lei (5.000 euros) after a ransomware attack exposed data of employees and customers.

key_findings: ANSPDCP says the breach was caused by a ransomware attack on the operator's IT infrastructure, through a remote connection without multi-factor authentication.
Data of a significant number of people, employees and customers, was affected, per ANSPDCP, including booking, SPA/wellness, billing and account data, and health information where collected.
Fine of 26.649 lei (5.000 euros) under GDPR article 32(1) and (2); investigation completed in October 2026.

summary: Romania's data protection authority ANSPDCP said on 17 November it fined Turism Lotus Felix SA 26.649 lei, the equivalent of 5.000 euros, under GDPR article 32. According to ANSPDCP, a ransomware attack via a remote connection without multi-factor authentication exposed data of employees and customers, including booking, billing and possibly health data. Bihon.ro reports the company runs a hotel in Băile Felix.
title: Romania's ANSPDCP fines Băile Felix hotel operator after ransomware attack

evidence.quote: TURISM LOTUS FELIX SA a fost sancționată cu amendă în cuantum de 26.649 lei, echivalentul a 5.000 EURO.

validation.note: ANSPDCP (dataprotection.ro) and Bihon.ro each state the fine and the ransomware attack. Primary: ANSPDCP's own press release of 17 November read; Bihon.ro (23 November) relays it and adds that the company operates a hotel in Băile Felix. ANSPDCP gives no count of affected people and no date of the attack.
